rules.title: Repeated failed logons

breakdown.label: Repeated failures within the configured window

rules.why: The failure threshold was met for the same account, source, and reporting host within one time window.
rules.benign: Mistyped passwords or stale service credentials can cause bursts.
next: Confirm the account owner and source device.
Compare source IP, reporting host, logon type, and nearby endpoint activity.
Check for stale service credentials and approved authentication tests.

rules.title: Possible password guessing followed by success

breakdown.label: Repeated failures within the configured window
Subsequent matching successful logon in that window

rules.why: Repeated failures were followed by success for the same account, source, and reporting host; known logon types are compatible.
rules.benign: A legitimate user can succeed after correcting a password.
next: Confirm the account owner and source device.
Compare source IP, reporting host, logon type, and nearby endpoint activity.
Check for stale service credentials and approved authentication tests.

rules.title: Possible password spraying across accounts

breakdown.label: Distinct targeted accounts from one source and host within the window

rules.why: One source targeted at least the configured number of distinct accounts on the same reporting host.
rules.benign: Authentication testing, shared proxies, or misconfigured applications can produce this pattern.
next: Confirm the account owner and source device.
Compare source IP, reporting host, logon type, and nearby endpoint activity.
Check for stale service credentials and approved authentication tests.

rules.title: New account granted group membership

breakdown.label: New account
Group addition
Matching identity and host within the configured window

rules.why: A new account was added to a security group within the configured window on the same reporting host.
rules.benign: Approved onboarding or service setup can include both changes.
next: Verify the target account and actor against an approved change.
Confirm the group privileges and intended account lifetime.
Review subsequent logons and endpoint activity for the account.

rules.title: New account granted group membership

breakdown.label: New account
Known privileged group name or SID
Matching identity and host within the configured window

rules.why: A new account was added to a recognised privileged group within the configured window on the same reporting host.
rules.benign: Approved privileged onboarding or service setup can include both changes.
next: Verify the target account and actor against an approved change.
Confirm the group privileges and intended account lifetime.
Review subsequent logons and endpoint activity for the account.

rules.title: User account created

breakdown.label: Account creation event

rules.why: A new account was created and needs ownership and purpose checks.
rules.benign: Routine onboarding and test accounts are common.
next: Verify the target account and actor against an approved change.
Confirm the group privileges and intended account lifetime.
Review subsequent logons and endpoint activity for the account.

rules.title: User account deleted

breakdown.label: Account deletion event

rules.why: An account was deleted.
rules.benign: Approved offboarding and cleanup are common.
next: Verify the target account and actor against an approved change.
Confirm the group privileges and intended account lifetime.
Review subsequent logons and endpoint activity for the account.

rules.title: Security group membership changed

breakdown.label: Group addition event

rules.why: A member was added to a security group.
rules.benign: Approved access changes are common.
next: Verify the target account and actor against an approved change.
Confirm the group privileges and intended account lifetime.
Review subsequent logons and endpoint activity for the account.

rules.title: Privileged group membership changed

breakdown.label: Known privileged group name or SID

rules.why: A member was added to a recognised privileged group.
rules.benign: An approved administrative access request can explain the change.
next: Verify the target account and actor against an approved change.
Confirm the group privileges and intended account lifetime.
Review subsequent logons and endpoint activity for the account.

rules.title: Security audit log cleared

breakdown.label: Security log clearing removes local audit history

rules.why: The Security log was cleared, reducing locally available investigation history.
rules.benign: Authorised maintenance can include clearing logs.
next: Identify the actor and maintenance record.
Check forwarded logs and endpoint evidence around the clearing.
Confirm logging continued afterward.

rules.title: Windows service installed

breakdown.label: Service installation event

rules.why: A service was installed and may run automatically.
rules.benign: Software installers and updates commonly install services.
next: Verify service name, image path, publisher, account, and approved change.

rules.title: PowerShell encoded-content cue

breakdown.label: Encoded command switch or Base64 conversion in PowerShell context

rules.why: The command or script contains an encoded-command switch or Base64 conversion.
rules.benign: Legitimate automation can use encoded content.
next: Review the full command or script and the parent process.
Confirm the script author, source, and approved purpose.
Gather endpoint evidence before deciding whether to escalate.

rules.title: PowerShell download-and-execute cue

breakdown.label: Download and dynamic evaluation patterns in one PowerShell record

rules.why: The same command or script contains download and dynamic evaluation expressions.
rules.benign: Approved bootstrap scripts and deployment tooling can use this pattern.
next: Review the full command or script and the parent process.
Confirm the script author, source, and approved purpose.
Gather endpoint evidence before deciding whether to escalate.

rules.title: Office application launched a shell or script host

breakdown.label: Office parent and shell/script-host child paths in the same process record

rules.why: An Office application is recorded as the creator of a shell or script host.
rules.benign: Approved macros and add-ins can launch these tools.
next: Review the full command or script and the parent process.
Confirm the script author, source, and approved purpose.
Gather endpoint evidence before deciding whether to escalate.

rules.title: Script host command references a remote resource

breakdown.label: mshta or regsvr32 command with a remote resource argument

rules.why: The recorded script-host command includes a remote HTTP resource argument.
rules.benign: Some approved legacy deployment tools can use remote resources.
next: Review the full command or script and the parent process.
Confirm the script author, source, and approved purpose.
Gather endpoint evidence before deciding whether to escalate.

rules.title: User account locked out

breakdown.label: Account lockout event

rules.why: Windows recorded an account lockout.
rules.benign: Mistyped passwords or a stale stored credential can lock an account.
next: Confirm the account owner and source device.
Compare source IP, reporting host, logon type, and nearby endpoint activity.
Check for stale service credentials and approved authentication tests.

rules.title: Explicit credentials used for a logon attempt

breakdown.label: Explicit-credential logon attempt event

rules.why: An application attempted a logon using explicitly supplied credentials; this event alone does not establish success.
rules.benign: RunAs, scheduled work, and management tools commonly use explicit credentials.
next: Verify the subject, credential account, target server, and process.
Look for related successful or failed logons on the target.

rules.title: Scheduled task created

breakdown.label: Task creation event

rules.why: A scheduled task was created.
rules.benign: Installers and approved automation commonly create tasks.
next: Review the task name, full task XML, run account, actions, triggers, and approved change.

rules.title: Scheduled task updated

breakdown.label: Task update event

rules.why: A scheduled task was updated.
rules.benign: Approved automation and software maintenance can update tasks.
next: Compare the task definition with the approved version and check its actor.

rules.title: Scheduled task deleted

breakdown.label: Task deletion event

rules.why: A scheduled task was deleted.
rules.benign: Cleanup and software removal can delete tasks.
next: Verify the task name and deletion against approved maintenance.

rules.title: System audit policy changed

breakdown.label: Audit policy change can affect evidence collection

rules.why: System audit policy changed; inspect the logged subcategory and change values to determine the effect.
rules.benign: Group Policy and approved hardening can change audit settings.
next: Review the subcategory and change values.
Verify the actor and approved policy change.
Check whether expected events continued to be collected.

rules.title: Windows Firewall rule changed

breakdown.label: Firewall rule change event

rules.why: A local firewall rule was added, modified, or deleted; the Event ID identifies the action.
rules.benign: Installers, administrators, and approved policy changes can alter rules.
next: Review the rule name/ID and profile.
Check the resulting firewall policy and approved change.

rules.title: Windows Firewall setting changed

breakdown.label: Firewall setting change event

rules.why: A firewall setting changed; the logged setting and value need interpretation.
rules.benign: Approved policy or network configuration changes can explain the event.
next: Review the setting type, value, and profile.
Confirm the resulting firewall state and authorised change.
